coarse_skill_concept: Download a Windows OS image and install or run it inside a QEMU virtual machine, configuring disk images, boot flags, and hardware emulation parameters.

task_judgments.reason: Requires compiling a specific QEMU version, launching qemu-system-i386 with a pre-existing disk image in snapshot mode, configuring VNC on :1/5901, and setting up nginx on port 80 — all core parts of the candidate skill.

Requires creating a raw disk image with qemu-img, booting an ISO through qemu-system-x86_64 to run an unattended installer, configuring VNC on :1/5901, and setting up nginx on port 80 — directly covered by the candidate skill.

final_groups.skill_concept: Launch a legacy Windows OS inside QEMU by creating/configuring a disk image, invoking qemu-system with appropriate CPU/memory/VGA flags, exposing a VNC display on port 5901, and proxying it via nginx on port 80.
final_groups.reasoning: Both tasks share the same end-to-end procedure: obtain or use an existing OS image, run qemu-system with BIOS-compatible settings, bind VNC to display :1 (port 5901), and front it with an nginx web interface. The XP task adds an unattended installation phase, but that is a natural extension of the same skill rather than a different skill entirely.
